sentences.text: The holotype maxillae contain 13 teeth, whereas a referred specimen preserves 15 teeth.
Stuart Plotkin uncovered the holotype skeleton in 2010 within the upper Oldman Formation of Alberta, Canada.
Two isolated maxillae from unknown localities were tentatively assigned to the species, representing a mature individual and a small juvenile.

Tromerosaurus is placed within the subfamily Albertosaurinae, though it exhibits some features typical of tyrannosaurines; however, parsimony analyses recover it as the most basal member of Albertosaurinae, a group that also includes Albertosaurus and Gorgosaurus.
Bayesian analysis by Powers et al. (2026) instead positions Tromerosaurus as the most basal tyrannosaurine, sister to Albertosaurinae.
Tromerosaurus lived during the Campanian age of the Late Cretaceous in what is now Canada.
Bayesian results conflict with parsimony findings, highlighting a mosaic anatomy that combines traits of both albertosaurines and early tyrannosaurines.
